does: Cooks a thin round of atta dough for a short time on each face on a dry, hot iron plate, then lays it straight on the open flame, where the steam inside swells it into a soft ball. The finished bread is brushed with ghee and kept soft under a cloth.
how: Heat the iron plate until it is hot all over. A dusting of flour dropped on it should brown at once.
Lay the rolled round on the hot plate. When small bubbles show on the top, turn it.
Cook the second face until it has pale brown spots.
Using tongs, lift the bread off the plate and lay it straight on the open flame. It puffs up in moments.
Turn it over for a moment, then take it off. Brush it with ghee if wanted and stack the finished breads in a cloth, so that they stay soft.

cues.text: Bubbles rise on the upper face, then the bread swells like a ball on the flame, with brown flecks.
The finished bread is soft and flexible, not stiff or leathery.
A warm, toasty scent of wheat rises, with no burnt smell.

mistakes.mistake: Cooking it too long on the plate, so that it dries out and will not puff.
mistakes.fix: Turn it as soon as bubbles show, and keep each side short.

mistakes.mistake: Putting it on a plate that is not hot enough, so that it turns leathery.
mistakes.fix: Heat the plate until a dusting of flour browns at once.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the bread on the flame, where it chars to ash.
mistakes.fix: Hold it there for moments only and turn it.

comes_after.why: The rolled round has to be thin and even or it will not puff.

variant_of.differs: After the dry plate the bread is lifted off and held directly on the open flame, where trapped steam puffs it into a ball. A griddled flat bread is left on the hot surface from start to end.
